findings.description: Adding Method M increased average ROUGE-L for every reported paired KD loss: GKD from 20.17 to 22.51, KLD from 18.10 to 19.70, and SRKL from 21.44 to 22.94; the table note reports the same average-direction result for four omitted losses.

For each displayed KD loss, Method M improved ROUGE-L on all five evaluation sets, so the improvement was consistent across the 15 shown loss-by-dataset comparisons, with GKD having the largest reported average gain at 2.33 points.

The strongest displayed student by average score, SRKL with Method M, remained 0.50 ROUGE-L below the teacher overall, although it exceeded the teacher on VicunaEval and S-NI and remained below it on the other three sets.
In the KLD ablation, full Method M achieved the highest ROUGE-L on every evaluation set among plain KLD and all ablated variants.

The easy-to-hard curriculum ordering alone, with both adaptive schedules removed, did not improve KLD consistently: it scored lower than plain KLD on four of five sets and only 0.09 points higher on SelfInst.

The component results identify the rising temperature schedule as the main driver and the supervised-ratio schedule as an additional contributor: removing temperature produced scores below plain KLD on all five sets, retaining temperature but removing the ratio schedule improved all five, and restoring the ratio schedule increased all five again.

The evidence is limited to the included GPT-2 results and descriptive seed means: no standard deviations or significance tests are reported, the number of independent training runs is unstated, and the analogous OPT table is not included.
